plan.summary: JWT auth lifecycle with refresh token support: URL QueryString token extraction, localStorage persistence, INMA JWT direct decode, 401 interceptor with automatic refresh and concurrent handling, welcome endpoint proxy.
plan.q_intent: URL'de QueryString ile access token ve refresh token saklayarak apiden jwt token ile istek yap, 401'de refresh token ile yenile, logout'ta temizle, welcome endpoint'ine istek yap ve cevabi ekrana yaz.
plan.interview_notes: Refresh: INMA kendi refresh endpoint'i var (testapi.wapcrm.net/api/token/refresh). Storage: localStorage. JWT decode: INMA JWT direkt decode, exchange flow kaldirildi.

files_changed.change: ValidateOpsAuth INMA JWT fallback, refresh proxy endpoint, welcome proxy endpoint, login endpoint returns INMA tokens + refresh_token
Added RefreshUrl and ApiBaseUrl to InmaAuth section
Full rewrite: localStorage token storage, jwt-decode, 401 interceptor with concurrent refresh, InmaTokenClaims interface, welcome endpoint
URL token extraction (accesstoken+refreshtoken), welcomeData state, logout clears localStorage

build.command: dotnet build InvektoServis.sln + tsc --noEmit + vite build

verification_questions.question: Does the 401 interceptor correctly handle concurrent requests that all receive 401, ensuring only one refresh call is made?
Are both access_token and refresh_token properly cleared from localStorage on logout, and does the login page correctly redirect?
Does the URL token extraction properly sanitize the URL (removing tokens from browser history) and handle missing refreshtoken gracefully?
Does ValidateOpsAuth correctly try INSE JWT first then INMA JWT as fallback, preventing unauthorized access if neither validates?
Does the refresh proxy endpoint properly validate inputs, handle INMA service unavailability, and prevent token leakage in logs?

non_goals: Adding JWT protection to ops endpoints

user_facing_errors: Refresh token gecersiz veya suresi dolmus
error_handling.silent_failure_explanation: All catch blocks either return explicit values (false/null) triggering logout, or set user-visible error state. Welcome endpoint failure is intentionally silent (non-critical).
